The Madrid derby stands out as easily the biggest fixture of the La Liga season so far, with Atlético Madrid looking to overtake Real Madrid in the early standings.

Match News and Current Form

Atlético Madrid come into the derby in fine form, with Wednesday’s 4-0 thrashing of Osasuna, following a 3-0 success over Real Sociedad last weekend. Diego Simeone’s men have made a relatively smooth start to the campaign considering the upheaval caused by the Julián Alvarez saga in the summer to sit on 13 points, a tally they last bettered after six games of a La Liga season back in 2021/22 when they were reigning champions! Real actually went on to win the title that season, but Atleti will be confident of landing a heavy hit on their rivals here given that they’ve won three of their last four home matches without conceding (D1).

Real Madrid may sit two points better off than their hosts here having won five of their six league games (L1), but performances in recent matches have left a lot to be desired. Real needed a late winner to see off Elche after they’d squandered a two-goal lead, leaving boss José Mourinho to lament his side’s inability to take “chances to put matches beyond reach”. The legendary Portuguese manager is taking on Atleti for the first time in over 12 years and has lost just one of his eight meetings with them as Real manager (W8, L1), a record he’ll hope to lean on given that Los Blancos have won just four of their last nine competitive away games (D1, L4).

Head-to-Head History

Real have lost just two of the last eight H2Hs in all competitions (W3, D3), and could win three successive Madrid derbies for the first time since December 2020 here. Los Blancos were beaten 5-2 here last term in La Liga, with Atlético losing just one of the last seven league meetings they hosted (W3, D3).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Ten of Atlético’s 14 league goals this term arrived after half-time.

Atlético won the corner count in 11 of their last 13 home league matches.

Ten of Real Madrid’s last 11 La Liga wins in Sunday-held away games were accompanied by a clean sheet.

Seven of Real Madrid’s last ten away league games featured at least six yellow cards.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Jonathan David has directly contributed to three goals in his last two games for Atlético (G2, A1) and has won each of the last 11 club level games he scored in. Kylian Mbappé has followed up a record-breaking World Cup by scoring eight goals in seven games for Real this season, though just one of those came on the road and his two prior scoring appearances against Atlético failed to yield a victory (D1, L1).

Alvarez and Pablo Barrios have missed Atleti’s last two games, while Real look to have no fresh issues.

Betting Analysis

Real have looked shaky on the road recently, and given their relatively large outsiders status, backing Atlético to win looks very tempting.

Author: Ryan Fisher
